summary: Orgyen Jikdral Chöying Dorjé studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Shechen Gyaltsab.
Orgyen Tendzin Norbu studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and later taught Shenphen Nangwa.
Oriane Lavolé is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Stanford University, where she was a PhD candidate in 2020 and attested as a doctoral student in 2026.

Orion Klautau works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a B.A. from the University of São Paulo by 2002 and a Ph.D. from Tohoku University by 2010, where he served as Associate Professor in 2015.

Orna Almogi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute, under Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam in 1995, and under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen. Her posts include the University of Hamburg and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Osamu Hayashima is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and at the University of Hamburg in 1992. He held professorships at Nagasaki University, Shiga University of Medical Science, and Ryukoku University.
Osamu Izumoji works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held academic posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

Osamu Oba was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Kansai University, he held posts at Kansai University (circa 1968–1998), Kogakkan University (circa 1998–2002), and the University of the Sacred Heart.

Osamu Takata specialized in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology, studying under Baiei Henmi. He served as a lecturer at Tohoku University (attested 1961) and as department director at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (attested 1967).

Osborn Bergin was a linguist who studied at University College Cork, the School of Irish Learning, and the University of Freiburg, under Kuno Meyer and Heinrich Zimmer. He held posts at University College Dublin (~1909–1940) and Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (~1940–1941).
Oscar Botto was an Indologist who studied under Mario Vallauri and founded the journal Indologica Taurinensia.

Oscar Flex worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as a missionary for the Gossner Evangelical Lutheran Church in 1861, worked with the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts in 1877, and was superintendent for the East-India Tea Company.

Oscar Lewis was an Indologist educated at City College of New York (B.A. ~1932–1936) and Columbia University (Ph.D. ~1936–1940). He held posts at Brooklyn College, Washington University in St. Louis, the University of Washington, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

Linguist and Indologist Oscar Luis Chavarria-Aguilar studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D. ~1949–1952). He held posts at Deccan College, American University in Cairo, University of Michigan, University of Rochester, City College of New York, and National University of Costa Rica.

Oskar Frankfurter worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Göttingen (Ph.D. ~1872–1874). He founded the Siam Society in 1904, directed the National Library of Thailand (1905–1917), and taught Thai at the University of Hamburg.

Oskar Johann Wiedemann was a linguist who studied under Leo Meyer at the University of Tartu, earning a Magister and a Ph.D. He later served as a Privatdozent at the University of Tartu from 1887 to 1890.

Oskar Kressler was a scholar of Japanology and Indology. He studied at Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, Geneva, and Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann (Ph.D. ~1900–1904). He later served as Privatdozent (1932) and associate professor of Japanology (1939–1949) at the University of Bonn.

Oskar von Hinüber is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Mainz under Karl Hoffmann and Paul Thieme. He held posts at Mainz (1965–1981) and Freiburg (1981–2006), and directed the Nepal Research Centre.

Osmund Bopearachchi studied at the University of Kelaniya, CNRS, Panthéon-Sorbonne University (Ph.D. ~1983–1987), and Paris-Sorbonne University. He served as Emeritus Director at the CNRS (1989) and as an adjunct professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~2014).

Osvald Sirén was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology who earned his doctorate at the University of Helsinki. He was a professor at Stockholm University (1908–1923), taught at Harvard and Yale, and worked as a curator at the Guimet Museum and Nationalmuseum.
